target_customer: UK households that pay for energy and do not switch supplier
problem: Households overpay on energy because switching is tedious, so loyal customers drift onto expensive tariffs.
business_model: Commission from energy suppliers on auto-switched customers, free to consumers

technical_complexity.rationale: Tariff comparison and switching automation depend on supplier data and process handling more than novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: Several auto-switchers launched in 2018 and incumbents with comparison traffic could copy the idea.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: GoCo Group, owner of GoCompare, bought it in July 2019 to complement its own weflip auto-switching service.

market_need_then: The Dragons' Den segment (Aug 2018) saw all five Dragons make offers, and press covered the product as a way to switch energy suppliers without effort.

branding.community_and_virality: Dragons' Den appearance in August 2018 produced a record low equity deal and broad UK press.

brand_strength.rationale: The TV appearance drove national press and a record low equity headline, but no sources show lasting brand awareness before the sale.

outcome_analysis: Look After My Bills went from YC Winter 2018 to a Dragons' Den deal in August 2018 and a sale to GoCo Group in July 2019 for up to 12.5 million pounds including earn-out. Fast publicity and a clear consumer saving story let it exit within a year, while later coverage says its energy switching was paused as supplier deals dried up in the cost of living crisis.
notes: Website returns HTTP 410. Round is GBP 120,000 for 3% of equity from Dragons Den (City AM), no USD figure recorded. One outlet says GBP 100,000 (outlier). Startupintros lists a $120K seed from Altair and LETA in Jan 2018, single aggregator, unverified. Exit price: up to GBP 12.5m including earn-out per Simmons & Simmons and Sharecast; early press said GBP 8.5m. Auto-switching competitors (Flipper, Switchd, Switchcraft) appear in undated guides so the list is left empty. Founding year not stated.
